mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate remains unchanged for two consecutive months above 5%, market expectations of future rate cuts decline, lowering real discount rates and boosting equity present-value pricing, which drives a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 5% and two consecutive months of no change
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the 30-day moving average of the same period in the prior month (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% month-over-month coincides with a 2-day decline in Treasury yields, signaling inflation surprise and prompting equity price adjustments that produce a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL month-over-month increase > 0.5% and GS10YR 2-day change < -0.1%
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns underperform the 30-day moving average by more than 5 percentage points in the same inflation regime.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in employment growth (PAYEMS) above 200,000 jobs per month for three consecutive months is accompanied by a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE), strengthening consumer demand and supporting a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 200000 for 3 consecutive months and UNRATE < previous month
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward return is negative despite all trigger conditions being met and no major exogenous shock (e.g., oil price spike).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) unexpectedly exceeds prior month by at least 2% and coincides with a decline in retail sales (HOUST) of more than 1%, it signals a shift from inventory building to consumption-driven demand, which is associated with a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO month-over-month increase > 2% and HOUST month-over-month decrease > 1%
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward return is negative in > 40% of such triggered events across 3 years of data.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial supply measured by RSAFS of more than 10% month-over-month, following a prior expansion, is interpreted as a supply-side shock that raises uncertainty and compresses forward discounting, producing a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS month-over-month increase > 10% followed by month-over-month decrease > -5%
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns remain non-negative in all such episodes after controlling for macroeconomic confounders.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent monetary easing (FEDFUNDS < 1% for four consecutive months) lowers real rates and increases risk appetite, leading to a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 trading days in a non-stagflationary regime.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from the 30-day moving average in the same regime.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in job openings (PAYEMS) exceeding 600,000 for a single month while unemployment (UNRATE) remains below 4% signals a tight labor market that supports wage growth and consumer confidence, resulting in a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward return is negative despite all trigger conditions and no major exogenous negative shock (e.g., oil price spike).

mechanism_narrative: When the inflation-adjusted GDP deflator (CPIAUCSL - GDP deflator proxy) unexpectedly increases by more than 0.4% month-over-month, it suggests persistent demand pressures that outpace supply, which is associated with a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward return is positive in > 60% of such events across 5 years of data.
